question: Who was the first President of the Swaraj Party in 1922-23? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Chittaranjan Das
Subhash Chandra Bose
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi
Jawaharlal Nehru
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chittaranjan Das

Explanation:
The Swaraj Party was founded on January 1, 1923, by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru. Its formation was a result of the differences between the Pro-changers and No-changers within the Indian National Congress after the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement. The party aimed to enter the legislative councils and challenge the government from within. Chittaranjan Das was the first President of the Swaraj Party, while Motilal Nehru served as its Secretary. The party achieved significant success in the 1923 elections, emerging as the largest party in the Central Legislative Assembly. This party is considered one of the earliest experiments in parliamentary politics in India.

☛ Date of formation of Swaraj Party → January 1, 1923
☛ Main objective of Swaraj Party → Enter legislatures and oppose the government
☛ First Secretary of Swaraj Party → Motilal Nehru
☛ Result of Swaraj Party → Became the largest party in 1923 elections
question_hi: 1922-23 में स्वराज पार्टी के प्रथम अध्यक्ष कौन थे? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))

Explanation:
स्वराज पार्टी की स्थापना 1 जनवरी 1923 को चित्तरंजन दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू ने की थी। इसका गठन असहयोग आंदोलन के स्थगन के बाद कांग्रेस के भीतर परिवर्तनवादी (Pro-changers) और नो-चेंजर्स (No-changers) मतभेदों के कारण हुआ। पार्टी का उद्देश्य विधान परिषदों में प्रवेश करके सरकार को अंदर से चुनौती देना था। स्वराज पार्टी के प्रथम अध्यक्ष चित्तरंजन दास थे, जबकि मोतीलाल नेहरू सचिव बने। पार्टी ने 1923 के चुनावों में महत्वपूर्ण सफलता प्राप्त की और केंद्रीय विधानसभा में सबसे बड़ा दल बनी। यह पार्टी भारतीय राजनीति में संसदीय राजनीति के शुरुआती प्रयोगों में से एक थी।

question: Which of the following was related to the first Anglo-Maratha war? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Treaty Salbai
Treaty of Madras
Treaty of Paris
Treaty of Mangalore
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Treaty Salbai

Explanation:
The First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782) was fought between the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire. This war ended with the Treaty of Salbai (1782), signed between Warren Hastings and Nana Fadnavis. Under this treaty, both parties restored each other's territories and established peace for 20 years. The Treaty of Madras (1769) is related to the First Anglo-Mysore War, the Treaty of Paris (1763) to the Seven Years' War, and the Treaty of Mangalore (1784) to the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

☛ Governor-General at Treaty of Salbai → Warren Hastings

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन प्रथम आंग्ल-मराठा युद्ध से संबंधित था? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options_hi: संधि सालबाई

पेरीस की संधि
मैंगलोर की संधि
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संधि सालबाई

Explanation:
प्रथम आंग्ल-मराठा युद्ध (1775-1782) ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी और मराठा साम्राज्य के बीच लड़ा गया था। यह युद्ध सालबाई की संधि (1782) के साथ समाप्त हुआ, जिसे वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स और नाना फड़नवीस के बीच हस्ताक्षरित किया गया। इस संधि के अनुसार, दोनों पक्षों ने एक-दूसरे के क्षेत्रों को वापस कर दिया और 20 वर्षों की शांति स्थापित हुई। मद्रास की संधि (1769) प्रथम आंग्ल-मैसूर युद्ध से, पेरिस की संधि (1763) सात वर्षीय युद्ध से, और मंगलोर की संधि (1784) द्वितीय आंग्ल-मैसूर युद्ध से संबंधित है।

question: Who asked Gandhi to pay attention to the problems of farmers in Champaran? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Shivaram Rajguru
Prince Shukla
Vallabhbhai Patel
Bhagat Singh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prince Shukla

Explanation:
The Champaran Satyagraha was a landmark event in India's freedom struggle. In 1917, a peasant named Rajkumar Shukla (also known as Prince Shukla) met Mahatma Gandhi and apprised him of the miserable condition of farmers cultivating indigo in Champaran. Gandhi agreed to his request and arrived in Champaran, where he studied the farmers' problems and led the satyagraha against the British. This was Gandhi's first successful satyagraha movement in India.

question: When did the Santhal rebellion break out? (RRB JE CE (29/08/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: 1855
1912
1895
1821
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1855

Explanation:
The Santhal rebellion broke out in 1855, a major tribal uprising against the British East India Company led by the Santhal tribe. The rebellion was spearheaded by brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu. The primary causes were oppressive British policies, including land confiscation, high taxes, and forced labor. The rebellion spread across the Santhal Pargana region, now in Jharkhand. The Santhals employed guerrilla warfare tactics, but the British army brutally suppressed the uprising. Although the rebellion failed, it became a symbol of tribal resistance against colonial rule. The year 1855 marks its beginning.

question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact carried out? (RRB JE EE (19/09/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: 1941
1930
1940
1931
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1931

Explanation:
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin. Under this pact, the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn, and Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference. The pact included the release of political prisoners, relaxation of salt laws, and return of confiscated property. However, the pact proved short-lived as the British government did not fulfill its promises. This agreement was a significant phase in the Indian freedom movement.

question: The demand for the Constituent Assembly was put forward by the Indian National Congress in 1936 at its session held at- (RRB JE (29/05/2019) Shift 2 CBT 1)
options: Faizpur
Bombay
Kanpur
Lahore
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Faizpur

Explanation:
In 1936, the Indian National Congress held its annual session at Faizpur (Maharashtra) under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru. This session is historically significant because it formally proposed the demand for a Constituent Assembly to frame India's constitution. The Congress declared that the constitution should be drafted by a body elected by the people of India. This marked a shift in the freedom struggle, emphasizing self-determination. The Faizpur session was notable for being the first Congress session held in a rural area, focusing on peasant and worker issues. The demand later materialized in 1946 when the Cabinet Mission Plan led to the formation of the Constituent Assembly.

☛ Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly formed? → Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)

question: Who wrote the lyrics of the song 'Sare Jahan Se Achcha'? (RRB JE CBT I (01/06/2019) Shift 2)
options: Rabindranath Tagore
Kavi Pradeep
Mohammed Iqbal
Munshi Premchand
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mohammed Iqbal

Explanation:
The lyrics of the song 'Sare Jahan Se Achcha' were written by the renowned poet and philosopher Mohammed Iqbal. This patriotic song was composed in 1904 and later published in his book 'Bang-e-Dara'. It symbolizes the diversity and unity of India and was written to instill a sense of patriotism among Indians during his time. The song is still sung on national occasions like Independence Day and Republic Day. Mohammed Iqbal is also known as 'Shair-e-Mashriq' (Poet of the East).

question: Who among the following religious and social reformers contributed in the abolition of Sati in 1829? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)

Raja Rammohan Roy, often called the Father of Indian Renaissance, played a pivotal role in the abolition of the Sati practice in 1829. question: In which year did King George V and Queen Mary of Britain visit India, and the announcement regarding the transfer of India's capital from Calcutta (Kolkata) to Delhi take place? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 3)
